_comment: AI services' providers, models and dated prices (D225). Data, not code: add a model, retire one (retiredOn), add a newer price table (a later 'effective' day wins from that day on) or change a licence or data term here, with the day it was checked. Each model belongs to one kind of work. 'rank' is MetaRush's own order of how good a model's results are within its kind (higher is better, from the providers' own descriptions); it is shown with every estimate's alternatives, never a hidden score. Prices are US dollars per 'unit' (picture, second, minute, hour, song, thousand-characters, request), 'byOption' by a picture's size; Google's prices add what is sent, in tokens. A provider whose 'route' is 'local' runs its models on this computer: no key, no money, nothing leaves it (D278). A provider whose 'route' is 'gateway' would serve other providers' models (its models naming it in 'via'); none is built (D224). A model reachable only through a gateway names it in 'onlyVia' (D282): it is listed with its terms, never offered, chosen or sent. Generated video's models stay in internal/videogen/catalog.json.

data.summary: On a Google project with billing turned on, Google doesn't use what you send or what it makes to improve its products, and keeps them only for a limited time to look for misuse. On the free tier Google may use them to improve its products, and people at Google may read them. MetaRush asks Google not to keep its requests and deletes the files it uploads right after use.
data.training: Not on a project with billing turned on; on the free tier Google may use what you send to improve its products.
data.retention: Logged for a limited time to look for misuse. Requests MetaRush sends aren't kept (store: false); files it uploads are deleted after use (Google deletes them after two days anyway). Voice copies are kept for a year after their last use, until MetaRush deletes them.
data.region: Any country where Google or its agents have facilities.

data.summary: D-ID erases what its API is sent within 24 hours unless asked to keep it, and doesn't look at it for any purpose, training its models included, while it is stored. A presenter stays at D-ID until it is deleted. MetaRush deletes each clip, the sound sent for it and the voice D-ID copies from a training take right after use, and deletes the presenter and D-ID's consent record when the presenter is retired.
data.training: Not while it is stored; D-ID's biometric privacy policy says what it keeps of a face isn't used to train its models.
data.retention: API uploads erased within 24 hours unless kept on purpose; links to finished clips last 24 hours; a presenter and its consent record stay until deleted.

presenters.takeAdvice: At least a minute of the person speaking naturally to the camera, in one take (two or three minutes is better), well lit and steady; filmed against a green screen when you want a colour behind the presenter.
presenters.backgrounds: A colour behind the presenter only when its training take was filmed against a green screen; otherwise the take's own background.
presenters.deletes: Deleting a presenter at D-ID removes it; D-ID's docs don't say whether the training footage it fetched goes with it (its uploads are erased within 24 hours unless kept).
presenters.erasure: To have D-ID erase what it keeps about a person's face, ask D-ID as its biometric privacy policy says (https://www.d-id.com/biometric-privacy-policy/).

stock.summary: D-ID's API pages don't say which plans license its stock presenters for commercial use, client work or ads, so MetaRush doesn't offer them.

models.title: D-ID Express

licence.summary: D-ID's terms license what its paid plans make for commercial use; its trial and personal plans are for personal use and carry a watermark. Its API pages don't list which plan is which.

notes: D-ID reads up to 5 minutes of sound a clip.
The clip keeps the training take's shape. D-ID's scene reference names no transparent background, so a presenter made against a green screen gets a colour behind it (green to key out later).

models.title: D-ID Express

licence.summary: A person's presenter is theirs to use only with their consent; D-ID's terms bar impersonating anyone and are for people 18 or older.

notes: D-ID checks the person reading its consent words, with their passcode, against its own text before it makes the presenter.
Training takes D-ID five to ten minutes.

prices.note: D-ID sells minutes in monthly plans and doesn't show their prices on its own pages; this is the cheapest plan for commercial use divided by its minutes, as others list it on 25 Oct 2026. Check your plan.
D-ID's pages don't say that making a presenter uses minutes.

data.summary: HeyGen's privacy policy lets it use what you send to improve its services and train its models unless the account asks it not to; deleted data goes within about 72 hours of a request and stays in its backups 60 days. MetaRush deletes each clip and the sound sent for it right after the download.
data.training: Yes, unless the account opts out by writing to HeyGen's privacy team; its Enterprise customers' data is governed by their contracts.
data.optOut: Ask HeyGen's privacy team to opt the account out of training, as its privacy policy says (https://www.heygen.com/privacy).
data.retention: Uploads and videos stay until deleted; deleted within about 72 hours of a request, then 60 days in backups.

presenters.takeAdvice: HeyGen makes a person's own presenter only after they record its consent on HeyGen's own page, which MetaRush can't take people through yet.
presenters.backgrounds: Any colour behind a stock presenter.
presenters.deletes: Deleting a video at HeyGen removes it; the sound uploaded for it is deleted on its own.
presenters.erasure: To have HeyGen erase what it keeps about a person, ask HeyGen as its privacy policy says (https://www.heygen.com/privacy).

stock.summary: HeyGen says its stock avatars are cleared for commercial use, ads, marketing, social media and client work on eligible paid plans; it doesn't say which plans are eligible.

models.title: HeyGen Avatar IV

licence.summary: HeyGen says videos made on its paid plans may be used commercially; its free plan adds a watermark.

notes: HeyGen reads up to 10 minutes of sound a clip.
Some of HeyGen's stock presenters are withdrawn from time to time; MetaRush says so when one is.

prices.note: HeyGen's pricing article gives $0.05 a second for Avatar IV photo presenters and its Enterprise table counts its studio presenters the same; its self-serve rate card for stock presenters didn't load. Check your balance.
